title: Collaborative Editing
summary: Collaborative editors like Google Docs or Figma let several people type into the same document at once and still end up with identical copies. Each keystroke is applied locally right away and sent as an operation. A session server puts every operation for a document in one order, adjusting it for concurrent edits (OT) or merging it with a conflict-free data type (CRDT), and broadcasts it, so every copy converges.

walkthrough.title: Type locally, send an op
walkthrough.text: Alice types 'x' at position 5. Her editor shows it immediately (no waiting on the network) and sends insert('x', 5) tagged with the document revision it was based on.

walkthrough.title: Order and transform
walkthrough.text: The document's session server gives the op the next sequence number. If Bob's concurrent insert at position 2 landed first, Alice's op is transformed to position 6 so it still means the same thing.

walkthrough.title: Persist before acknowledging
walkthrough.text: The op is appended to the document's operation log. Only then is it acknowledged, so an acknowledged edit is never lost.

walkthrough.title: Broadcast to collaborators
walkthrough.text: Bob's editor receives the transformed op and applies it. Every client applies the same ops in the same order, so all copies converge.

walkthrough.title: Acknowledge and rebase
walkthrough.text: Alice gets her ack with the new revision. Any ops she typed meanwhile are rebased onto it, which is invisible to her.

walkthrough.title: Share cursors and presence
walkthrough.text: Cursor positions and 'who's here' go over a separate lossy channel. They are sent many times a second, never stored, and losing one is harmless.

walkthrough.title: Snapshot and compact
walkthrough.text: Every few hundred ops the server writes a full snapshot. A new joiner loads the latest snapshot plus the ops after it, instead of replaying years of history.

data.label: Editor (Alice)
responsibilities: Applies the user's edits instantly (optimistic local apply).
Keeps a queue of sent-but-unacknowledged ops and rebases them on incoming changes.
Works offline and syncs the queue when reconnected.

failureModes.scenario: Long offline period with many edits
failureModes.mitigation: CRDTs merge any order deterministically; show a 'changes merged' notice.

failureModes.scenario: Client bug applies an op differently
failureModes.mitigation: Periodic checksums against the server; reload from snapshot on mismatch.

data.label: Editor (Bob)
responsibilities: Applies remote ops in server order.
Transforms remote ops against his own pending ones.

failureModes.scenario: Missed op after a brief disconnect
failureModes.impact: A gap in sequence numbers, so the state is wrong.
failureModes.mitigation: Reconnect with the last seen revision; the server replays the missing ops.

failureModes.impact: Falls far behind a fast-typing team.
failureModes.mitigation: Batch ops; jump forward via snapshot if too far behind.

data.label: Document Session Server

input.name: Client ops
input.type: Ops from every editor of doc 123

responsibilities: Is the single place that orders ops for a document.
Transforms or merges concurrent ops so they converge.
Broadcasts committed ops and acks to all connected editors.

failureModes.impact: Editors of its documents are briefly disconnected.
failureModes.mitigation: Another server takes over the doc, rebuilds from snapshot + log, and clients resume by revision.

failureModes.scenario: Two servers think they own the same doc
failureModes.impact: Two orderings, so the document forks.
failureModes.mitigation: Lease-based ownership with fencing tokens on log appends.

data.label: Presence & Cursors

output.name: Fan-out
output.type: Latest presence per user in the doc

responsibilities: Shares who is viewing and where their cursor is.
Keeps only the latest state, dropping stale updates.
Expires users who disconnect without saying goodbye.

failureModes.impact: The log fills with cursor noise.
failureModes.mitigation: Keep presence entirely separate and ephemeral.
Throttle and show only active editors' cursors.

data.label: Operation Log

input.name: Append
input.type: (docId, rev 42, op, author, ts) IF rev = 41

responsibilities: Durably stores every op in order: the document's full history.
Rejects appends that skip or duplicate a revision.
Powers version history and 'see who changed this'.

failureModes.impact: Acks slow down; editing feels laggy for everyone.
failureModes.mitigation: Batch appends; keep the log close to the session server.

failureModes.impact: Large storage and slow loads for old documents.
failureModes.mitigation: Snapshots plus archiving old ops to cold storage.

data.label: Snapshot Store

input.name: Compaction
input.type: State at rev 4000 built from previous snapshot + ops

output.name: Load
output.type: Snapshot + tail ops for opening a doc

responsibilities: Stores periodic full copies of each document.
Makes opening a document fast regardless of its history length.
Provides restore points for version history.

failureModes.mitigation: Verify by replaying; fall back to the previous snapshot plus more ops.
Trigger compaction by op count, not just time.
